Regular Council Meeting
CITY OF SOLANA BEACH
ACTION AGENDA
The Action Agenda of the City Council Meeting is a document provided immediately following the Council Meeting in order for staff and the public to be aware of the business transacted and actions taken by Council. This is a preliminary draft and not a public record. The meeting's legal record is the Minutes approved by the City Council.
SOLANA BEACH CITY COUNCIL
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY and PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY
Joint REGULAR Meeting
WEDNESDAY, MAY 25, 2011
6:00 P.M.
CITY COUNCIL CHAMBERS
635 S.HIGHWAY 101
SOLANA BEACH, CALIFORNIA
The City Council acts as the City of Solana Beach Redevelopment Agency and the Public Financing Authority.
NOTICE
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, persons with a disability may request an agenda in appropriate alternative formats as required by Section 202 of the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990. Any person with a disability who requires a modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should direct such request to the City Clerk's office at (858) 720-2400 or by email at least 72 hours before the meeting.
As a courtesy to all meeting attendees, please set cellular phones and pagers to silent mode and engage in conversations outside the Council Chambers.
The Regular Meetings of the City Council are scheduled for the 2nd and 4th Wednesdays and are broadcast live on Cox Communications, Channel 19, and Time Warner, Channel 24. Council meetings are archived and available for viewing. The video taping of meetings are maintained as a permanent record and contain a detailed account of the proceedings.
A full City Council agenda packet with backup information is available at City Hall, at the Solana Beach branch of the San Diego County Library (157 Stevens Ave.), and online www.ci.solana-beach.ca.us at least 72 hours prior to the meeting. Agenda related writings or documents regarding an agenda item and that are received after the distribution of the agenda but at least 1 hour 30 minutes prior to the meeting will be available for public viewing at City Hall and posted online with the agenda.

CITY OF SOLANA BEACH
Regular Council Meeting
Solana Beach City Council, Redevelopment Agency, and Public Financing Authority
MINUTES
JOINT REGULAR MEETING
Wednesday, May 25, 2011
06:00 P.M.
City Hall Council Chambers, 635 S. Highway 101, Solana Beach, California
The City Council acts as the City of Solana Beach Redevelopment Agency and the Public Financing Authority.
CALL TO ORDER AND ROLL CALL:
Mayor Heebner called the meeting to order at 6:23 p.m.
Present:
Heebner, Kellejian, Roberts, Nichols, and Campbell.
Absent:
None.
Also Present:
David Ott, City Manager
Johanna Canlas, City Attorney
Angela Ivey, City Clerk
Dennis Coleman, Finance Director
Wende Protzman, Dir. Admin. Serv/Deputy City Mgr
Tina Christiansen, Community Dev. Dir.
Mo Sammak, City Engineer/Public Works Dir.
APPROVAL OF AGENDA:
MOTION: Moved by Roberts and seconded by Nichols.
Motion carried unanimously.
ORAL COMMUNICATIONS:
This portion of the agenda provides an opportunity for members of the public to address the City Council on items relating to City business and not appearing on today’s agenda by submitting a speaker slip (located on the back table) to the City Clerk. Comments relating to items on this evening’s agenda are taken at the time the items are heard. Pursuant to the Brown Act, no action shall be taken by the City Council on public comment items. Council may refer items to the City Manager for placement on a future agenda. The maximum time allotted for each presentation is THREE MINUTES (SBMC 2.04.190). Please be aware of the timer light on the Council Dais.
Richard Brenckman said that he was a business owner in Solana Beach, that he led the Compassion Project, led the Council through a non-vocal exercise to help the Council seek a sense of peace with the belief that it will help the Council make decisions from a place of compassion, and handed out Compassion Cards.
Gwen Ford stated that she was for chickens in Solana Beach, that she grew up with chickens, she believed they promoted good health, that fresh eggs tasted delicious, and urged the Council to think carefully about the topic when it came up.
Lincoln Quintana pointed out supporters of chickens in the audience, urged Council to move forward in regards to the chicken ordinance, stated that Del Mar, Santa Barbara, Carlsbad, and San Diego allowed chickens with no home value depreciation, that he had personal experience with chickens and knew they were not a nuisance and did not create odors in small quantities, and that they were less safety threats from birds than from cats and dogs, according to the CDC website.
Council and Staff discussed the fact that the City of Del Mar did not allow chickens and that the leader of this topic requested a six month postponement.
Mark Bannach, president of the HOA at Santa Fe Hills northeast side, read a section of their CC&Rs, pointing out a particular section regarding the banning of farm animals. He stated that each CC&R of each Association supersedes the Solana Beach decision, and that they will have police enforce the CC&R banning chickens.
COMMUNITY ANNOUNCEMENTS:
Council reported community announcements.
COMMENTARY:
Council made commentary remarks.
A.
CONSENT CALENDAR: (Action Items) (A.1. - A.7.)
Items listed on the Consent Calendar are to be acted in a single action of the City Council unless pulled for discussion.
Any member of the public may address the City Council on an item of concern by submitting to the City Clerk a speaker slip

Recommendation: That the City Council

Adopt Resolution 2011-045 authorizing the City Manager to execute a Professional Services Agreement, in the amount of $20,908, with T.B. Penick & Sons, Inc. for concrete site work surrounding Fletcher Cove Community Center building using the Lithocrete concrete paving process.
MOTION: Moved by Roberts and seconded by Nichols.
Motion carried unanimously.
NOTE: The City Council shall not begin a new agenda item after 10:30 p.m. unless approved by a unanimous vote of all members present. (SBMC 2.04.070)
B.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: (B.1.- B.2.)
This portion of the agenda provides citizens an opportunity to express their views on a specific issue as required by law
after proper noticing by submitting a speaker slip (located on the back table) to the City Clerk .
After considering all of the evidence, including written materials and oral testimony,
the City Council must make a decision supported by findings and the findings must be supported by substantial evidence in the record.
An applicant or designees for a private development/business project, for which the public hearing is being held,
is allotted a total of fifteen minutes to speak, as per SBMC 2.04.210. A portion of the fifteen minutes may be saved to respond to those who speak in opposition.
All other speakers have three minutes each. Please be aware of the timer light on the Council Dais.
B.1.
Development Review Permit (DRP) and Structure Development Permit (SDP) for 305 Clark Street, Applicant: Mathew Nikolaus, Case #17-10-21. (File 0600-40)
The proposed project meets the minimum objective requirements under the SBMC, is consistent with the General Plan and may be found, as conditioned, to meet the discretionary findings required as discussed in this report to approve a DRP and administratively issue a SDP. Therefore, Staff recommends that the Council:
1.
Conduct the Public Hearing: Open the public hearing, Report Council disclosures, Receive public testimony, Close the public hearing; and
2.
Find the project exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act pursuant to Section 15303 of the State CEQA Guidelines; and
3.
If the Council makes the requisite findings and approves the project, adopt Resolution 2011-048 conditionally approving a DRP and an administrative SDP to construct a new two-story, single-family residence at 305 Clark Street Avenue.
David Ott, City Manager, introduced the item.
Rich Whipple, Principal Planner, presented a powerpoint (on file) reviewing the project.
Council and Staff discussion ensued regarding the heights of the storypoles, that some exact heights were difficult to achieve with certain types of materials but that the storypole heights were achieved, and whether some storypoles had fallen down.
Mayor Heebner opened the public hearing.
Council reported their familiarity with the project.
Mr. Shultz, applicant, stated that he would pass on a presentation.
Pete Meeker said that he owned a property on Clark St. 1978 and was strongly opposed to the project, that the project was huge and fitting to the community and neighborhood, that he had turned in a 6 page letter, that he had submitted a letter that was not included in the package to Council, that he the neighborhood was unique and that this building did not fit in, and asked Council to reject it.
Council and Staff discussed the decision by Staff regarding the correspondence that was received during the SDP process, which was an administrative process, and prior to the DRP process which was a different design review and approval, that there may had been some miscommunications between Staff and the Meekers when asking them to submit a letter for the DRP process and referring to the prior letter that was already on record, which was part of the prior SDP process, and that the current design in this DRP process was a modified design from the prior process, and whether Council could receive all correspondence during the last 12 months on a project, and that Council’s determination in this discretionary process during the public hearing should be considered separately, and that Staff needed to be more clear about the differences between the two processes and related submittals and paperwork.
Gary Martin stated that there was no way for the public to know which version was being presented or when it had changed, that what happened in this neighborhood could affect his neighborhood affecting architects and designers understanding of what is acceptable, that it was a cumulative impact because structures were approved and each one changes the structure of the community, that the bulk and scale was not compatible, that it would be appropriate for an urban neighborhood but was not appropriate for this low scale neighborhood, and that the architect was talented, and that he could provide a good redesign.
Gene Walker said that there was a similar issue in the past, that Solana Beach was very unique, that it was huge place shoe horned into a lot, that it was not compatible with the scale of the neighborhood, and that no house should be an island.
Scott McKenna presented a powerpoint (on file) and said that he lived north of property and and that views would be lost with this project and that he opposed the approval fo the project.
Council and Mr. McKenna discussed whether he had considered filing for view assessment, that he did not understand the time frame so he was not able to meet it, that views were not part of this consideration, and he confirmed that he had concerns about the bulk and scale in relation to the surrounding area being completely out of proportion.
John Murk stated that he owned his property for 20 years, that he was the first JPA manager in Cardiff, that he supported the project, that the City had a reasonable plan and process of going about how to build and review and approval, that Staff would not make the recommendation because they felt like it, that the owner had spent a lot of money and time to develop it, that the bulk and scale of the bluff area are completely different than other areas so there were various areas in the neighborhood, and that there was a system set up to follow.
Torgen Johson stated that the City tried codify the qualitative cumulative affects of development with Proposition A across Solana Beach, that the view assessment process allowed a person to explore the full envelope as well as work with neighbors to scale back, that the architects are told to maximize the square footage which changes the character of the place, and that this project could be redesigned and scaled back within the character of the area.
Joe Ford said that he lived off of Cliff and Hwy 101, that he noticed the story poles and had sympathy for the neighbors, that while it met the floor area ration that not all lots were shaped the same, that this project was over limit, and that it was larger than typical.
Bart Zeigler stated that the project was outsized for the neighborhood, that the scale greatly exceeded the homes in the neighborhood, and asked Council to protect the character of community.
Ted Schultz, applicant architect, said that the applicant wanted to build their dream home, that all neighbors were contacted as required, that many close neighbors were contacted above and beyond, that they met with the Meekers regarding their concerns regarding views and altered the 2nd story and pulled back as well as added glass panels to block views from this property into their backyard, that they understood that any two-story would create shadows so the issue shifted towards the Meekers backyard, that there was no other strong opposition, that 14 people commented in writing recently, that there was a list of 12 properties that go beyond the square footage, that privacy was also important to the owner, and passed out a list of properties (on file) that he said were larger in the direct area, and that the project was supported by many local residents.
Julian Pachoni, said that he had been helping the applicant on the project for a year, that they had been working with neighbors, the plans had been at the City for 8 months, and all of a sudden hearing from people with issues, that working with Staff towards these issues and taking Staff’s recommendation have shown efforts to address all interests, that the Meeker's letter was not included because his issues had been addressed and then last minute he had new opposition, that story poles had been up since February, that there were several homes with a larger lot coverage than this project, that there was no definition of what the character of the neighbor was, and that he thought the character was defined by the anti-mansionization rules Council had approved and that they had met all of those.
Council and the speaker discussed the 11 support letters and that it appeared that 4 were duplicates and that it was not fair that Mr. McKenna would get to present his view issues since he never filed for it and it turned into a bulk and scale issue this evening when it was clear that his only issue was view.
MOTION: Moved by Roberts and seconded by Nichols to close the public hearing.
Motion carried unanimously.
Mayor Heebner stated that the project was a Development Review Permit and that the City’s code had 2 aspects regarding these permits, one was dealing with floor area ratio, which was reduced during the Proposition A discussion, and the other was the Development Review Permit which required the confirmation of findings, that one of those findings is discretion, so the City’s code provides for both quantitative numbers as well as discretion of community character, regarding bulk and scale, and that the recommendation cites both of these issues.
Councilmember Roberts stated that he agreed with Mayor Heebner providing clarification on the process and findings, that this project was out of scale with the neighborhood, that it appeared that the applicant was heading in the right direction but not where they need to be, that it was out of character with the neighborhood, and that he could not findings 2.a. (adjacent land use) and 2.b. (building and structure placement) and that he would motion to deny without prejudice in order to allow the applicant and architect to address the concerns, and that he had concerns about not having all information at their hands regarding the entire process.
Mayor Heebner stated that to deny without prejudice allowed the applicant to not have to go to the back of the line and could go right away once the redesign was ready.
Councilmember Nichols stated that the pie wedged lot forces the facade to be projected out, that Mr. Schultz was a talented architect, that he had found creative ways in other projects to address this issue, that the Meeker's concern seemed valid because of the side elevation, that there was an opportunity to improve the neighborhood and that the scale and bulk of this project was out of character, and that he could not make finding 2.a. (adjacent land use) and could second the motion.
Mayor Heebner said that she agreed with the concerns expressed, that she had issue mostly with the north and east elevation, that the facade was so plain and it needed some articulation of interest or something to give the building interest within the architectural style, that she understood that many homes would be redeveloped due to small size, that approvals created a cumulative effect, and that she would not make finding 2.a. (adjacent land use).
Councilmember Campbell said that he agreed with the comments, that the process is fair since the voters voted for it, that Council had an obligation to apply these discretionary aspect, that the decisions were not made lightly, that anyone at the last minute had the right to address the Council in a public hearing regarding a project, that there was a basis for the process, that Council had the right to ask any questions including views, and that he was not soliciting any specific information but had the right to ask questions of applicants and those speakers from the public.
Deputy Mayor Kellejian stated that he had been critical of the process and that he hoped that someday there would be a toolkit or criteria to help Council make these judgements like the view assessment process, that it was difficult at times to judge bulk and scale, that he understood that the applicant had done everything they could to be before Council, that he could judge a project on a blank wall, that he had stated before that he would not want to live next to a blank wall, that the north elevation was an issue since the applicant could improve it with some articulation, and that he would agree with other comments to have the applicant return with a redesign.
MOTION: Moved by Roberts and seconded by Nichols to deny the project without prejudice.
Motion carried unanimously.
Mayor Heebner recessed the meeting at 7:50 p.m. and reconvened at 7:56 p.m.
Councilmember Nichols recused himself due to living within 500 ft. of the project.

Mayor Heebner opened the public hearing.
Council disclosed their familiarity with the project.
Gary Cohn, architect, said that they had met and listened to the community, that they had formulated the design based on th back and forth dialogue with the community, that they had arrived at a design compatible with the neighborhood, that they had reduced the project by more than 1000 sq ft, that the garage had been somewhat submerged, that the set back was increased to exceed the minimum requirements, that one bedroom was eliminated from each unit due to the concern about additional parking, that the test story poles were used to show that the 2nd story mass had been moved as far south as possible, that it was highly articulated, and that it was a compatible project.
Gary Martin said that he previously opposed this project and had met with the applicant on many occasions, that he now supported the project, that it was rare to meet with an owner and architect who listened and was collaborative, that the project looked nice and was compatible, that it was a pleasure to work with them, and that Joe Ford stated that he also supported the project.
Tim Coughlin stated that he agreed with the support of the project, that both the applicant and the architect did a great job.
